newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg Q2 may beat views, other food results mixed.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg Q2 may beat views, other food results mixed.

text.p: Cereal giant Kellogg Co is expected to report above-consensus earnings for the second quarter, analysts said, not only outpacing last year's depressed earnings but also approaching what it made in 1995.
"I think the company will try to match the $0.77 earned in 1995," Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said, adding her estimate for Kellogg is $0.75 a share.
Overall, food companies are expected to report mixed quarterly results, analysts said.
The First Call consensus of earnings estimates for Kellogg is $0.72 a share, above last year's results of $0.45 that were hurt by price cuts in the U.S. cereal industry.
"I'm hopeful that they'll beat the consensus," added CS First Boston analyst Michael Mauboussin, who estimates quarterly earnings of $0.77 a share, matching the 1995 level.
He said Kellogg benefited from higher U.S. cereal volume, strength in its convenience foods and a profit contribution from international businesses overall.

Kellogg spokesman Anthony Hebron declined to comment on anticipated results for the second quarter, other than to reiterate that the company hopes to post low double-digit earnings per share growth for all of 1997.
Among the other food companies reporting quarterly results, meat processor IBP Inc is expected to post second quarter results that are sharply below a year-ago due to poorer beef and pork margins.
"This was a very tough quarter," Ghez said, adding her estimate of $0.35 a share remains below the current First Call consensus of $0.58.
CPC International Inc is expected to report roughly flat second quarter earnings, including results for the corn refining business that it plans to spin off.

Quaker Oats Co, which recently completed the sale of its Snapple beverage business, is expected to report higher second quarter earnings thanks to its food businesses. Its U.S. Gatorade sports drink sales could be flat, analysts said.

Sara Lee Corp is projected to report about a 10 percent increase in earnings for its fiscal fourth quarter, largely as a result of margin improvements and cost cutting, said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Tim Ramey said.
Ralcorp Holdings Inc is expected to report a narrowed net loss for its fiscal third quarter.
